mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q-o-q for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% in the same month indicates a successful disinflationary tightening, which supports equity valuations by reducing inflation risk premia and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% AND CPIAUCSL falls >0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -1% m-o-m AND HOUST < -1% m-o-m in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 new jobs per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between the real savings rate (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns: higher real savings imply lower consumption, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of all trading days.
